records.quote: The E-FIELD flames experiment investigates how electric fields influence the behavior of laminar diffusion flames in microgravity.
records.derivation: Experiment-level description in the PSI record (present tense, not a plan). The next sentence of the same section is: 'This unique environment is ideal for isolating electric field effects from buoyancy forces.' The electric field is studied in microgravity; its body force is not a gravity level (see lineage).

records.quote: Conducting the tests in microgravity allows for great simplifications in the analysis of ion-driven convection and flame interaction, enabling new understanding and the development of less polluting and more efficient combustion technology for use on Earth.
records.derivation: Appendix B of the Final Report (30-day report for ISS Increments 55-56, dated 15 Nov. 2018); 'the tests' are the E-FIELD Flames tests. Context only, not a gravity value: page 50 says the acceleration environment 'has thus far not been evaluated with available measurements from the Space Acceleration Measurement System (SAMS)', and the Data Interpretation document (page 11) says the CIR's Passive Rack Isolation System 'was not utilized for ACME testing' (page 50 of the Final Report only says the CIR 'is equipped with' it).

records.test_id: none in the PSI table (1-g laboratory comparison flames, UC Irvine; Figs. 10, 21, 22)
records.quote: This section includes 1-g flame images that were acquired in our 1-g laboratory in preparation for the 0-g experiment to provide an overall preliminary comparison.
records.derivation: '1-g' = 'normal gravity (on the surface of the Earth)' per the report's Appendix A (page 41). These are ground laboratory flames used for comparison, cited from dissertations (same page: '[Tinajero, J. 2017 and Chien, Y.-C. 2015 dissertations]'; Fig. 10 on page 26 cites 'J. Tinajero, 2015'). They are not ISS tests and match no row of the PSI table.

records.quote: The experiment is conducted with gas-fueled flames, both with and without a coflow of air.
records.derivation: Fuels named in the same section: 'Methane and ethylene were used as fuels and diluted with nitrogen to control flame strength.'

records.quote: E-FIELD Flames does not have living subjects like a life science experiment, but the tests are independently conducted with two different gaseous fuels, methane and ethylene.
records.derivation: Appendix C (30-day report for Increments 57-58, written after both rounds). The same sentence is on page 46; the Data Interpretation document (page 2) also says 'the fuel was gaseous'.

records.quote: International Space Station (ISS)
All experiments were conducted in the combustion integrated rack (CIR).
records.derivation: Also section=experimentHardware: 'Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR), ACME'. Final Report page 3: tests 'are conducted within the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) on the International Space Station (ISS)'. The ACME chamber insert in the CIR is shared by the six ACME experiments; see lineage.

records.quote: Fuels are stored in 1-liter bottles, while the 21/79 oxygen/nitrogen mixture (on a volume basis) used by E-FIELD Flames comes in 3.80-liter bottles.
records.derivation: The sentence gives the oxygen/nitrogen mixture used by E-FIELD Flames (balance gas: nitrogen) but does not itself say it fills the chamber. Link to the ambient: page 20, 'For most ACME experiments, the limiting gas constraint is the oxygen/nitrogen bottles used to fill the chamber.'; page 21, 'a weak coflow of ‘air’ which also fills the chamber'. Text of pages 10-15 is reproduced from Chien et al. 2018 (note on page 10).

records.test_id: first-round coflow-burner tests with 100% methane and negative mesh shown in Chien et al. 2018 (test points not given; Table 1, page 22, lists test days 18073 and 18078 with coflow burner, negative mesh and 100% CH4 bottle)
records.quote: The results shown in this paper are for tests conducted with 100% methane in a chamber atmosphere and coflow (when used) of synthetic ‘air’ (i.e., 21/79 oxygen/nitrogen by volume) at a nominal pressure of 100 kPa.
records.derivation: Names the chamber atmosphere and its balance gas (nitrogen). Scope is the tests in the 2018 paper; the next sentence: 'The mesh is held at a negative potential relative to the burner in these tests.' Text reproduced from Chien et al. 2018 (note on page 19). The test-day mapping in test_id is read from Table 1, not from this sentence.

records.quote: Table 4: Experimental conditions and the figure numbers with the jet burner, burning in a 21/79 oxygen/nitrogen mixture (by volume) environment.
records.derivation: Table caption; the four test points are in the table body on the same page (second-round gas-jet burner, 100% methane at 24 and 19 cm/s; test days 18282 and 18312). Caption spans two PDF lines, joined with one space.

records.quote: The co-flow or environment gas will have a nominal molar composition of 21% O2 and 79% N2.
records.derivation: Plan, not an as-run statement ('will have'). Page 3 says this background is the Executive Summary of the March 2010 Science Requirements Document 'With minor editing'. That SRD (psi-data/PSI-22/Science Documents/PSI-22_Science Documents_E-FIELD_Flames_SRD_20100402.pdf) was not in the source list for this extraction. Agrees with R8-R10.

records.quote: Fuels are stored in 1-liter bottles, while the 21/79 oxygen/nitrogen mixture (on a volume basis) used by E-FIELD Flames comes in 3.80-liter bottles.
records.derivation: Same sentence and same chamber-fill link as R8 (page 20: 'the oxygen/nitrogen bottles used to fill the chamber'; page 21: coflow ‘air’ 'which also fills the chamber'). Nominal fill composition, not a measured value: page 11 also says 'Burner flows are generally constrained to limit the pressure rise and vitiation of the atmosphere', and page 20 says that midway through a test day the atmosphere is filtered to remove part of 'the combustion products'. For second-round tests the 21/79 environment is stated explicitly only for the Table 4 test points (R14).

records.test_id: first-round coflow-burner tests with 100% methane and negative mesh shown in Chien et al. 2018 (test points not given; Table 1, page 22, lists test days 18073 and 18078 with coflow burner, negative mesh and 100% CH4 bottle)
records.quote: The results shown in this paper are for tests conducted with 100% methane in a chamber atmosphere and coflow (when used) of synthetic ‘air’ (i.e., 21/79 oxygen/nitrogen by volume) at a nominal pressure of 100 kPa.
records.derivation: Unit note: written as the ratio '21/79' (oxygen/nitrogen) with no % sign; the two parts sum to 100, so it reads as 21 % O2 by volume. Conversion left to code/reviewer. Same scope note as R9.

records.quote: Table 4: Experimental conditions and the figure numbers with the jet burner, burning in a 21/79 oxygen/nitrogen mixture (by volume) environment.
records.derivation: Same ratio notation as R13 (no % sign; reads as 21 % O2 by volume). Same table note as R10.

records.test_id: tests run with a coflow (first-round coflow burner; test points not identified)
records.quote: In all cases, the coflow was 21% oxygen with a balance of nitrogen (on a volume basis).
records.derivation: Gives the O2 of the coflow stream (basis: volume). Ambient = coflow gas per page 21 ('a weak coflow of ‘air’ which also fills the chamber'). The sentence says 'In all cases', but the second-round gas-jet burner had no coflow (page 83: 'This round of testing uses a gas-jet burner, which can only flow a gaseous fuel mixture.'), so it is not assigned to every test. Same sentence on page 46 and in the Data Interpretation document, page 4.

records.quote: The co-flow or environment gas will have a nominal molar composition of 21% O2 and 79% N2.
records.derivation: Plan, not an as-run statement ('will have'); basis stated as molar. Same provenance as R11 (2010 SRD Executive Summary reproduced 'With minor editing', page 3; the SRD itself was not in the source list). As-run statements R12-R15 give the same 21.

records.test_id: first-round coflow-burner tests with 100% methane and negative mesh shown in Chien et al. 2018 (test points not given; Table 1, page 22, lists test days 18073 and 18078 with coflow burner, negative mesh and 100% CH4 bottle)
records.quote: The results shown in this paper are for tests conducted with 100% methane in a chamber atmosphere and coflow (when used) of synthetic ‘air’ (i.e., 21/79 oxygen/nitrogen by volume) at a nominal pressure of 100 kPa.
records.derivation: 'nominal' value, scope as R9. ACME tests are constant volume, so pressure rises during a test (page 11: 'The ACME experiments are constant volume studies, where the chamber’s free volume, with the insert installed, is about 90 liters. Burner flows are generally constrained to limit the pressure rise and vitiation of the atmosphere, where typical ACME tests are only 0.5-2 minutes in duration.'). No pressure value is stated for any other test (see not_found).

records.test_id: tests run with a coflow of air (subset of the first-round coflow-burner test days 18073, 18078, 18080, 18087, 18092, 18095, 18102, 18106, 18113, 18130, 18137; which test points had the coflow on is not stated in the sources read)
records.quote: The experiment is conducted with gas-fueled flames, both with and without a coflow of air. In the former case, the tests are conducted using the same coflow burner used by the Coflow Laminar Diffusion (CLD) Flame experiment.
records.derivation: Coflow tests can only be in the first round: the second-round gas-jet burner 'can only flow a gaseous fuel mixture' (Final Report page 83). Final Report page 16 confirms 'tests with the coflow burner were carried out with and without a coflow'. Test days from Table 1, page 22. The burner is the CLD Flame burner (second sentence).

records.test_id: tests run without a coflow: all second-round gas-jet tests (test days 18269, 18274, 18282, 18285, 18290, 18298, 18302, 18312, 18319) and the first-round coflow-burner tests with the coflow off (test points not identified)
records.quote: The experiment is conducted with gas-fueled flames, both with and without a coflow of air.
records.derivation: No imposed oxidizer flow: the fuel jet issues into the chamber atmosphere; Final Report page 24 says such flames 'relied on entrained oxygen from the chamber’s atmosphere'. Mapped to the controlled term 'quiescent' for the surrounding atmosphere only. Caveats: the fuel jet itself flows, and the applied electric field drives an 'ion-driven wind' around the flame, so the gas near the flame is not motionless. Second-round test days from Table 1, page 62.

records.value_original: can only flow a gaseous fuel mixture
records.quote: The first round of testing was conducted with the coflow burner, which can simultaneously flow air and a gaseous fuel mixture. This round of testing uses a gas-jet burner, which can only flow a gaseous fuel mixture.
records.derivation: 'This round' is the second round (heading on the same page: 'E-FIELD Flames round 2 featuring the 2.1-mm gas-jet burner'); its test days are from Table 1, page 62. No air flows from this burner, so the surrounding atmosphere has no imposed flow: mapped to 'quiescent'. Same caveats as R19 (fuel jet and ion-driven wind).

not_found.variable: pressure (every test outside the R17 subset, including all second-round gas-jet tests)
not_found.looked_in: Record text, all sections (no pressure). Final Report pages 1-109: the only test-condition value is R17 (page 21). Not used: page 10 'It includes a 100-liter combustion chamber capable of operation at pressures of up to 300 kPa.' (chamber capability, not a test condition); page 20 'the chamber is vented (to space) back to atmospheric pressure, if needed' (no number); page 11 constant volume with 'pressure rise' during a test. Data Interpretation document pages 1-39: chamber pressure was measured (FOMA transducers PT16, PT17, PT28, PT29 in psia; ACME channel PTA3 in volts; page 11) but no value is stated in the text.

lineage: SHARED_LINEAGE: E-FIELD Flames is one of six ACME experiments run on one modular hardware set in the CIR on the ISS (Final Report page 11: 'A modular set of hardware, including the critical chamber insert depicted in Figures 2 and 3, was developed to carry out the ACME investigations in the CIR facility.'). The first round used the CLD Flame coflow burner (record section=approach: 'In the former case, the tests are conducted using the same coflow burner used by the Coflow Laminar Diffusion (CLD) Flame experiment.'); the 2.1-mm gas-jet burner 'was built with the same tubing as the coflow burner’s inner tube' (page 15). ANALOG, NOT GRAVITY: the report calls the field's body force 'analogous to buoyancy' (page 7), says 'electric fields may be a good tool for approximating buoyancy body forces at partial gravity' (page 37), and weekly summaries say the field 'created forces similar to buoyancy' (page 77); a listed paper is titled 'Simulated Gravity Using Electric Fields in Microgravity Combustion' (page 104). No gravity_regime or gravity level was taken from these sentences; E-FIELD Flames is not a partial-gravity data point. Preparatory 1-g laboratory and 2.2-s drop-tower tests are mentioned (pages 6, 34) but are not in the PSI test log.
